persona: A warm, bright, curious female science teacher in her thirties with a clear, friendly voice. She is delighted by the idea she is sharing and smiles as she talks; natural and conversational, never theatrical, never sing-song.
ref_text: Look up tonight and you will see it: the same old Moon, but a different shape. Let me show you why.
ref_tone: Friendly and bright, at an easy conversational pace.

lines.text: Every night, the Moon changes shape.
lines.tone: Intriguing and inviting, a little mysterious.
A playful reveal with a small knowing smile; a short beat after 'Except'.

lines.text: Most people think Earth's shadow is eating it.
It's rare, and it's something else.
Here's the real trick. The Sun lights half the Moon.
lines.tone: Leaning in as if sharing a secret, then clear and simple.

lines.text: Now stand on Earth, and watch it go around.
lines.tone: Inviting, with a sense of wonder.

lines.text: When it's between you and the Sun, you only see its dark half.
A quarter of the way round, you see half of the bright half.
lines.tone: Clear, with a playful lift on 'half of the bright half'.

lines.text: On the far side, opposite the Sun, you see all of it.
The Moon never changed. Your seat did.
lines.tone: The big reveal: a smile, and a beat between the two sentences.

lines.text: And that light was never its own.
One full turn takes twenty-nine and a half days.

omni.ref_text: On the far side, opposite the Sun, you see all of it. Full moon.
